correctness.rationale: The square-zero algebra units decompose as N ⋊ T with both factors abelian. Dual arrow-block nonzero support S gives exact stabilizer |T_lambda|=(q−1)^c(S), orbit (q−1)^r(S), and support-size q^L product(q^{a_e}−1). Invariant radical characters extend to their inertia groups and the Clifford/little-group correspondence yields exactly (q−1)^c(S) irreps of degree (q−1)^r(S) per dual orbit. Thus the displayed coefficients are exact for all finite quivers and prime-power q. The q=2 boundary and degree-square normalization are checked separately, and independent exact conjugacy class/dual orbit computations pass 19 configurations.

evidence: André–Dias proves general compact-induction of smooth representations over non-Archimedean local fields, not exact finite-field character multiplicities. The abstract Mackey/Clifford little-group theorem is a general known tool that the present work specializes and explicitly counts; its existence alone is not a pre-existing enumerative formula for all quiver patterns.

Halasi (2006) proves monomiality and the general degree shape q^r(q−1)^s for DN-algebra unit groups, while Theorem 1.3 identifies induction from subalgebra unit groups and Lemma 2.1 supplies the diagonal/radical decomposition. These statements do not count the number of irreducibles at each degree or give the weighted Tutte graph specialization.

value.rationale: Irreducible complex character-degree multiplicities are a canonical natural invariant of unit groups of finite algebras. The theorem completely determines them on the entire radical-square-zero split-basic/quiver family, including arbitrary loops, opposite arrow pairs and multiplicities, with orientation invariance and weighted Tutte/random-cluster evaluation. It yields new exact structural equalities for different algebras and a universal forest product. This is a coherent classification of an infinite natural family, not a relabeling of single numerical tables. Limits are explicit.
